project: PROVE - Verizon Smart Campus Innovation Challenge 2026-27 (Rutgers)

champion_thesis.name: PROVE: every lifeline Verizon moves arrives with proof it still reaches someone
champion_thesis.round1_hero: Plug-and-PROVE on Verizon's copper-replacement box (Voice Gateway if orderable, else Business Phone Connect / Inseego BPC100): the alarm panel's own test call is verified through Verizon's live network (handshake, checksum-valid message, kiss-off), plus signal at the spot (worst season), voice both ways, battery; a spoken/printed test-record receipt: GREEN / FIX AND RE-RUN / VISIT NEEDED
champion_thesis.value: lower self-install fallout on KPIs Verizon tracks (first-time-right, repeat dispatch <=30 days, care contacts per install, alarm households confirmed); ask = 30-day trial in one migration batch's self-install kits vs control; no invented dollars
champion_thesis.rutgers: Rutgers PROVE Lab in ECE (three-arm controlled bench with CIs); older-adult usability session; finals: elevator WHO ANSWERS pilot with Facilities (challenge-response, caller-ID continuity, time to a person vs 45 s)
video_rules: open on the stakes (keypad says SENT), not text cards
no dockets/rule sections/'paused'/'regulator stopped checking' in the video
only verified numbers (46k installed; 417k lines in two filings)
green receipt; test record, not a guarantee
never imply Verizon's network causes failures; failures go to the mentor first

Voice Connect (BPC100) guide: 'Compatibility is determined by your testing ... at time of install'; ##21 alarm-number registration; 3 AA batteries (3 h talk / 23 h standby); swap guide never mentions alarms

honest_negatives: Rutgers fire communicators (2020) and blue lights (2023) already off copper; main numbers on a CLEC: Rutgers is the proving ground, not a countdown
IP emergency phones already self-test audio; Deaf text mode already ships

Asterisk AlarmReceiver cannot decode SIA: no SIA claims
All alarm-delivery and signal thresholds are modelled until the bench measures them
